ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, exactly six congruent right-angled triangles are used to form two regular hexagons, one larger than the other. What is the ratio of the perimeter of the larger regular hexagon to that of the smaller one?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, \\
$\because$ $\triangle ABG \cong \triangle BCH$, \\
$\therefore$ AG＝BH, \\
$\because$ $\angle ABC=(6-2) \times 180^\circ \div 6=120^\circ$, $\angle CBH=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABG=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ AB＝$\sqrt{3}$AG, BG＝2AG, \\
thus BH＋HG＝2AG, \\
$\therefore$ HG＝AG, \\
$\because$ regular hexagon ABCDEF$\sim$regular hexagon HMNPQG, \\
$\therefore$ the perimeter of regular hexagon ABCDEF : the perimeter of regular hexagon HMNPQG = AB$\colon$HG = $\sqrt{3}$AG$\colon$HG = $\sqrt{3}$HG$\colon$HG = $\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as an outer regular hexagon ABCDEF and an inner regular hexagon HMNPQG, with the annular region split into six congruent right triangles. Use the local configuration near outer side AB: triangle ABG is congruent to adjacent triangle BCH, and points B, H, G lie on the same slanted side line of the smaller hexagon as shown. From congruence, AG = BH. Since the outer hexagon is regular, angle ABC = 120°. The right angle in triangle BCH gives angle CBH = 90°, so the remaining angle ABG = 30°. Thus triangle ABG is a 30-60-90 right triangle, giving AB = √3·AG and BG = 2AG. Because H lies between B and G, BG = BH + HG. Substitute BH = AG to get HG = AG. Therefore the perimeter ratio of the two regular hexagons equals their side-length ratio AB : HG = √3·AG : AG = √3.

method.method_draft: Read the figure as a large regular hexagon with side AB and a smaller regular hexagon inside it, with the six congruent right triangles filling exactly the area between them. Let the shorter leg of one right triangle be x. From the same local angle at an outer hexagon vertex, the right triangle has a 30° angle, so it is a 30-60-90 triangle; therefore the outer hexagon side is the longer leg, equal to √3x, and each right triangle has area (1/2)(x)(√3x) = (√3/2)x². The six triangles have total area 3√3x². The area of a regular hexagon of side a is (3√3/2)a². Hence the large hexagon area is (3√3/2)(√3x)² = (9√3/2)x². Subtracting the six triangle areas gives the small hexagon area: (9√3/2)x² - 3√3x² = (3√3/2)x². Therefore the small hexagon side length is x. The perimeter ratio is then the side ratio √3x : x = √3.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中可见一个较大的正六边形外框，内部还有一个较小的正六边形。大小两个正六边形之间的环形区域被分成六个形状相同的直角三角形，这些三角形首尾围绕小正六边形排列。

推理：按题设与图形，设每个直角三角形的短直角边为 x。由于大正六边形每个内角为 120°，在外六边形顶点处，直角三角形与正六边形边形成的锐角为 30°，所以该直角三角形是 30°-60°-90°三角形。于是其长直角边为 √3x，并且这条长直角边对应大正六边形的一条边，所以大正六边形边长为 √3x。

每个直角三角形面积为 (1/2)·x·√3x = (√3/2)x²，六个三角形总面积为 6·(√3/2)x² = 3√3x²。

正六边形边长为 a 时面积为 (3√3/2)a²。大正六边形面积为 (3√3/2)(√3x)² = (9√3/2)x²。小正六边形面积等于大正六边形面积减去六个三角形面积，即 (9√3/2)x² - 3√3x² = (3√3/2)x²。

因此小正六边形的边长满足 (3√3/2)s² = (3√3/2)x²，所以 s = x。正六边形周长比等于边长比，所以较大正六边形与较小正六边形的周长比为 √3x : x = √3。

正六边形边长为 a 时面积为 (3√3/2)a²。大正六边形面积为 (3√3/2)(√3x)² = (9√3/2)x²。小正六边形面积等于大正六边形面积减去六个三角形面积，即 (9√3/2)x² - 3√3x² = (3√3/2)x²。

因此小正六边形的边长满足 (3√3/2)s² = (3√3/2)x²，所以 s = x。正六边形周长比等于边长比，所以较大正六边形与较小正六边形的周长比为 √3x : x = √3。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, exactly six congruent right-angled triangles are used to form two regular hexagons, one larger than the other. What is the ratio of the perimeter of the larger regular hexagon to that of the smaller one?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, \\
$\because$ $\triangle ABG \cong \triangle BCH$, \\
$\therefore$ AG=BH, \\
$\because$ $\angle ABC=(6-2) \times 180^\circ \div 6=120^\circ$, $\angle CBH=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABG=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ AB=$\sqrt{3}$AG, BG=2AG, \\
thus BH+HG=2AG, \\
$\therefore$ HG=AG, \\
$\because$ regular hexagon ABCDEF$\sim$regular hexagon HMNPQG, \\
$\therefore$ the perimeter of regular hexagon ABCDEF : the perimeter of regular hexagon HMNPQG = AB$\colon$HG = $\sqrt{3}$AG$\colon$HG = $\sqrt{3}$HG$\colon$HG = $\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a larger regular hexagon, and inside it a smaller regular hexagon is enclosed by line segments; the annular region between the two is divided into six congruent right triangles. According to the markings in the problem and the method draft, the outer hexagon is ABCDEF, the inner hexagon is HMNPQG, and locally one can take two adjacent triangles ABG and BCH near the outer sides AB and BC, with H located on the segment from B to G. Reasoning: Since the six right triangles are congruent, △ABG ≅ △BCH, so the corresponding sides AG = BH. The outer hexagon is a regular hexagon, therefore interior angle ∠ABC = 120°. Also because △BCH is a right triangle, and the right angle taken by the method in the figure is ∠CBH = 90°, so ∠ABG = 120° - 90° = 30°. Thus △ABG is a 30°-60°-90° right triangle, obtaining AB = √3·AG, BG = 2AG. Because H is between B and G, BG = BH + HG. Substituting BH = AG and BG = 2AG, can get HG = AG. Both hexagons are regular hexagons, so the ratio of perimeters equals the ratio of side lengths, that is, larger regular hexagon perimeter : smaller regular hexagon perimeter = AB : HG = √3·AG : AG = √3.
